title: Turkish Comedian Deniz Göktaş Jailed Pending Trial Over Erdoğan 'Dictator' Joke
detail: Comedian Deniz Göktaş, 32, was detained for questioning at Istanbul Airport on July 2, 2026 upon returning from a trip abroad, days after prosecutors opened an investigation into a stand-up set — recorded in Istanbul and uploaded to YouTube on June 24 — that drew roughly 9.5 million views. In the routine, Göktaş described Erdoğan as having evolved from a 'shy dictator' to one 'confident in his identity,' and made a joke referencing the Quran. The Istanbul prosecutor's office received 185 complaints and charged him with 'publicly insulting religious values' and violating Article 299 of the Penal Code (insulting the president), an offense punishable by up to four years in prison. A court ordered him jailed pending trial on July 3. Free-speech advocates and fellow performers condemned the prosecution as an attack on comedic expression.
